A '''Murchason ring stress analyzer'''<ref name="Inside">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]''</ref> was a type of [[Color/Legends|silver]]-colored stress analyzer that consisted of a tube shaped body with spring shaped protrusion extending from the top. The [[Slavery|slave]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] kept a Murchason ring stress analyzer in his home in the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], on a ledge next to the workbench in [[Gender/Legends|his]] bedroom.<ref name="TPM" />

In [[32 BBY]],<ref name="Date">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], which includes the appearance of the Murchason ring stress analyzer, to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].</ref> Skywalker was using the workbench to build the [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], whose head rested on the ledge next to the stress analyzer as Skywalker brought [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] and the [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] in to his room to show off the [[Droid/Legends|droid]].<ref name="TPM" />

==Behind the scenes==
A Murchason ring stress analyzer first appeared in the [[1999]] [[prequel trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="TPM" /> The device was first named in [[2000]] reference book ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]'', which which was written by [[Kristin Lund]].<ref name="Inside" />
